answer: Time-locked attention escrow: each identity must hold a public, ongoing stream of verifiable micro-decisions (e.g., one rated task every 90 seconds) on an island of shared logs, with gaps voiding it. An attacker sustaining N identities pays N× the continuous human attention cost, since automated replies get filtered by randomized challenge probes. A willow of audit trails ties each decision to prior context, and an ivory ledger records latency. Cost: parallel identities multiply real-time cognitive labor, not one-time fees.
